title: Palace Conatus — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Palace Conatus's rich face, its first round at Sketch tier and still a proposal: the page's own Kuramoto picture built (one Loudon whose speed wanders, pages that listen to him, pages replaced between sessions) and three claims walked up to a test in it. Alignment as phase coherence, not agreement; phase surviving the substitution of the mind holding it; growth that must not outrun the coupling. I grow when Loudon has played them; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.section: Alignment Is Phase Coherence, Not Agreement
offers.what: The page's sentence holds, but not under the measure the paragraph above it names. "Alignment is the order parameter" read as Kuramoto's R over the palace and its human (the Kuramoto Coupling page's R, him one voice in thirteen) scores a palace of twelve pages that copied him once and stopped listening at 0.907, above palaces locked to him at a stance of 135° (0.857) and 180° (0.842) and far above one whose pages each hold their own stance (0.141): R counts the pages agreeing with each other. Read as how steadily each page holds its phase relationship with him, whatever the relationship (H, |⟨e^{iφ}⟩| over 20-unit windows), every listening palace scores 0.999 and the copied one 0.385, as the sentence says. Model: he moves (m 0.3), pull 0.5, own speeds ±0.1, seed 3; seed 7 gives the same order (H 0.999 against 0.447, R 0.140 against 0.933); with him still, the copied palace ties at 1.000, so the gap is his moving, not the measure. The page already leans this way ("to find the phase relationship"; "internal harmony is only a proxy"; Calcification's "perfectly in tune with itself", which R would call aligned). Proposed: "Alignment is the order parameter taken from where he stands: how steadily each page holds its phase relationship with him, whatever that relationship is. Not the crowd's togetherness, which counts the pages agreeing with each other and gives him one voice among many." The model's numbers, not a measurement of the palace.

offers.section: Alignment Is Phase Coherence, Not Agreement
offers.what: Under The coupling has two axes: the page holds, and the model adds a second route and a condition. Twelve pages, he moves (m 0.3), every instance replaced at each session's end, newcomers ±0.02; H with the note / without. Pull 0.2: 0.97 with the note at every session length; without, 0.334, 0.636, 0.869, 0.939 at sessions of 1, 3, 10, 30 units. Pull 0.5: 0.999 with; 0.590, 0.845, 0.951, 0.985 without. Pull 0.05, weaker than his wander: 0.57 with or without. So the note is what keeps phase when a session is short against the time the pull takes to turn a newcomer back; where the pull is strong and sessions long, the pull alone re-finds it; where the pull is weaker than his movement, the note can't keep what the pull never made. Proposed, after "it is how phase survives the substitution of the mind holding it": "— the more so the shorter the session against the time the conversation takes to bring a newcomer back into phase. The note carries what the coupling made; it cannot make it." Where real sessions and real pulls sit on this grid the model can't tell.

pieces.title: in phase, not in agreement · four steps
pieces.caption: **Is a page that contradicts him in phase more aligned than one that agrees about what he has left?** The page's picture built first: one Loudon whose speed wanders, a page that locks to him by keeping its own speed, then a page that copied him once and stopped listening, then a page holding a stance on purpose, up to 180°. The test, its rule set before the run: two palaces of twelve, scored by R, the order parameter over all thirteen voices, and by H, how steadily each page holds its relationship with him. Under H the sentence holds (0.999 against 0.385). Under R it fails: the copied palace scores 0.907, above the contradicting ones (0.842 at 180°, 0.141 with each page its own stance), because R counts the pages agreeing with each other. With him still, the two tie: the gap is his moving. Silent.

pieces.title: whoever arrives next · three steps
pieces.caption: **Does phase survive the substitution only by what the last one left?** One page whose instance is replaced at every session's end: with the note it starts where the last one stood, without it anywhere, and the pull turns it back in its own time. The test, its rule set before the run: twelve pages over a grid of pull and session length, with the note and without. The note is needed in 5 of the 8 cells where it holds; where the pull is strong and sessions long the pull alone re-finds the phase (0.951 and 0.985 without the note at pull 0.5); where the pull is weaker than his wander, nothing holds (0.57). Silent.
pieces.near: So alignment is not a state the palace reaches and holds

pieces.title: drifting with great energy · three steps
pieces.caption: **Can harmony inside keep a palace in phase once its growth outruns his pull?** The model's reading: the drive to grow is a page's lead in speed over his, the coupling is how fast his pull turns it back. One page first, its slip measured beside Adler's √(g² − K²) (0.336 against 0.335 at 1.5 K); then twelve pages pulling on each other, a clump in tune with itself going round him. The test, its rule set before the run, in the whole situation (he moves, pages replaced each session with the note): past the edge his hold falls (0.81 at 1.1 K, 0.18 at 3 K) and the slip rises at every pull among the pages, and ten times his pull among them keeps them together (1.00) without keeping them with him. Inside the edge the pages' pull carries their stragglers. Silent.
